displacements._about: Typical starting displacement (Phase 4). Shaft-type values describe the DISTAL part relative to the proximal part: shortening_mm, lateral_mm, posterior_mm, varus_deg (negative = valgus), apex_anterior_deg (negative = apex posterior), external_rotation_deg. Fragment-type values: away_mm (straight away from the fracture site), proximal_mm, use_impaction (use the impaction stored with a depressed fragment). Shortening is reduced automatically until the bone ends no longer overlap.

muscle.basis: Muscle pull (Phase 6d). Force of a muscle = its PCSA (all muscles equally active, as in spasm after a fracture). It acts at each attachment (model/<region>/muscles.json, from Z-Anatomy) along the muscle's own path. Forces on the fragments give the DIRECTION of the typical displacement; the SIZE is a teaching value (below). The leg (tibia, fibula, patella) moves with the femur fragment that carries the knee; the fragment that carries the femoral head turns in the acetabulum but does not move out of it. Not modelled: gravity, ligaments and capsule (except the patellar ligament, which holds the distal patella), wrapping of a muscle round bone further than its attachment, the bed. Sizes: Teaching values chosen by the engine author; no published source for the sizes.
